records.source: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־עָשָׂ֧ה הַיָּשָׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּדָוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: A son of twenty year[s] [was] Ahaz when he became king, and sixteen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and not he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh like David his father.
pieces: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his ancestor David had done.

L.1: Ahaz [was] twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like David his father.

R.1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, as his ancestor David had done.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 16:2, with one difference
decisions.reason: Chronicles repeats 2 Kings 16:2 almost word for word. Kings says "Yahweh his God"; Chronicles has only "Yahweh". As elsewhere, Chronicles leaves out the opening date by the reign of the king of Israel (2 Kings 16:1), and it names no mother for Ahaz, as Kings names none.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty years: twenty years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years. The numbers are hard to fit with the age of his son Hezekiah (29:1); see the note at 2 Kings 16:2.

decisions.choice: he did not do what was right ... like David: the good verdict denied
decisions.reason: The verdict given to the good kings is here turned into a denial. His father Jotham had received it (27:2). "David his father" means his ancestor David, the measure for every king of Judah.

decisions.choice: did not do the right in [the] eyes of / did not do what was right in the sight of / did not do what the LORD said was right; his ancestor
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 16:2 is kept at each level. Balanced and Readable say "ancestor" for "father", as they do wherever David is called the father of a later king.

records.heading: Ahaz king of Judah

records.source: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּדַרְכֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְגַ֧ם מַסֵּכ֛וֹת עָשָׂ֖ה לַבְּעָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he walked in [the] ways of [the] kings of Israel, and also cast images he made for the Baals.
pieces: He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; he also made images of cast metal for the Baals.

L.2: And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and he even made cast images for the Baals.

R.2: He lived the way the kings of Israel had lived. He even made metal idols for the Baals.

decisions.choice: the ways of the kings of Israel: as 2 Kings 16:3, with the idols added
decisions.reason: Kings says Ahaz walked in "the way" of the kings of Israel; Chronicles has the plural, "the ways". Chronicles then adds what Kings does not say here: that he made images for the Baals. To walk in someone's ways is to live as they did; the northern kings had served Baal since Ahab (1 Kings 16:31-32).

decisions.choice: cast images: idols made of molten metal
decisions.reason: The word names an image cast from melted metal, like the calf Aaron made (Exodus 32:4). The law forbids such images by name (Exodus 34:17; Leviticus 19:4).

decisions.choice: the Baals: Baal in his many local forms
decisions.reason: The plural names the god Baal as he was worshiped at many places and under many titles, as in Judges 2:11 and 2 Chronicles 17:3.

decisions.choice: lived the way; metal idols
decisions.reason: Readable says what "walked in the ways" means, as at 2 Kings 16:3, and calls the cast images "metal idols".

records.source: וְה֥וּא הִקְטִ֖יר בְּגֵ֣יא בֶן־הִנֹּ֑ם וַיַּבְעֵ֤ר אֶת־בָּנָיו֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ כְּתֹֽעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he made smoke in [the] valley of Ben-hinnom, and he burned his sons in the fire, according to [the] abominations of the nations whom dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.3: And he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and he burned his sons in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.3: He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and he burned his own sons in the fire as sacrifices. He copied the disgusting practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out of the land ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: burned his sons: where 2 Kings 16:3 has "made his son pass through the fire"
decisions.reason: Chronicles differs from Kings in three ways here. It adds that Ahaz burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom; it says "his sons", plural, where Kings has "his son"; and it says "he burned" where Kings says "he made pass through". In Hebrew the two verbs are spelled with the same three letters in a different order. Both name the same rite, the offering of children by fire (see the note at 2 Kings 16:3).

decisions.choice: he burned: the Hebrew text followed
alternatives: he made his sons pass through the fire
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "he made pass through" here, as in 2 Kings 16:3, perhaps from the same letters in the other order. The Hebrew text is followed; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Ben-hinnom: the valley south of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "The valley of the son of Hinnom" ran along the south and west of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:8). It became the place where children were burned (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31), and its name, Ge-hinnom, is the source of Gehenna. "His sons" may mean more than one son, or may name the practice in general; Hezekiah, at least, survived (verse 27).

decisions.choice: the abominations of the nations: the practices Deuteronomy forbids
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 18:9-12 forbids the abominations of the nations and names first anyone who makes a son or daughter pass through the fire. Yahweh drove out those nations because of such practices; the king of Judah now takes them up.

decisions.choice: detestable practices / disgusting practices; burned his own sons in the fire as sacrifices
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 16:3 is kept where the Hebrew is the same. Readable adds "as sacrifices" to say what the burning was (m1); it also adds "of the land" to say where the nations were driven from.

records.source: וַיְזַבֵּ֧חַ וַיְקַטֵּ֛ר בַּבָּמ֖וֹת וְעַל־הַגְּבָע֑וֹת וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And he sacrificed and made smoke at the high places and on the hills and under every tree luxuriant.
pieces: He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every leafy tree.

L.4: And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

R.4: He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the hilltop shrines, on the hills, and under every large, leafy tree.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 16:4
decisions.reason: This verse is word for word the same as 2 Kings 16:4, and the wording is kept. "Made smoke" means burned incense or offerings. The places echo Deuteronomy 12:2, which orders the destruction of the places where the nations served their gods "on the hills and under every leafy tree".

decisions.choice: high places (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֜הוּ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָיו֮ בְּיַ֣ד מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָם֒ וַיַּ֨כּוּ־ב֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁבּ֤וּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ שִׁבְיָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ דַּרְמָ֑שֶׂק וְ֠גַם בְּיַד־מֶ֤לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נִתָּ֔ן וַיַּךְ־בּ֖וֹ מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And gave him Yahweh his God into [the] hand of [the] king of Aram, and they struck him and took captive from him a captivity great and brought [them to] Damascus; and also into [the] hand of [the] king of Israel he was given, and he struck him a striking great.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God handed him over to the king of Aram. The Arameans defeated him, took a great many of his people captive and brought them to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him a heavy blow.

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram, and they struck him and took captive from him a great [number of] captives and brought [them to] Damascus. And he was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, and he struck him with a great striking.

R.5: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God let the king of Aram defeat Ahaz. The Arameans beat Ahaz's army, took many of his people as prisoners and brought them to Damascus. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} also let the king of Israel defeat him, and many of his men were killed.

decisions.choice: Yahweh his God gave him: the defeat is God's judgment
decisions.reason: Chronicles says plainly that Yahweh handed Ahaz over, because of the sins of verses 2-4, as it does for other kings who forsook him (12:5; 21:16; 24:24). "Was given" in the second half has the same sense: God is the one who gives.

decisions.choice: the war of Rezin and Pekah: battles that Kings does not tell
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:5 and Isaiah 7:1 tell how the kings of Aram and Israel besieged Jerusalem but could not take it. Chronicles tells of heavy defeats in the field during the same war. The city held, but the land and its army suffered.

decisions.choice: they struck him: the Arameans struck Ahaz's forces
decisions.reason: "They" is plural after "the king of Aram": his army is meant. "Him" is Ahaz, standing for his kingdom and army. In the second half "he" is the king of Israel.

decisions.choice: gave into the hand of: handed over to the power of
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. To give someone into another's hand is to let him be defeated by him.

decisions.choice: the Arameans; his people; Ahaz's army; the LORD also let; many of his men were killed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who struck and who was captured (m3). Readable puts the passive "he was given" as "the LORD also let" (m1), and says what the great blow was, as verse 6 goes on to tell.

records.source: וַיַּהֲרֹג֩ פֶּ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֜הוּ בִּֽיהוּדָ֗ה מֵאָ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד הַכֹּ֣ל בְּנֵי־חָ֑יִל בְּעָזְבָ֕ם אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And killed Pekah son of Remaliah in Judah one hundred and twenty thousand in day one, all [of them] sons of valor, because they had forsaken Yahweh, God of their fathers.
pieces: In one day Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 in Judah, all of them valiant men, because they had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

L.6: And Pekah son of Remaliah killed in Judah 120,000 in one day, all of them sons of valor, because they had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers.

R.6: In a single day Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 soldiers of Judah, all of them brave fighting men. This happened because the people of Judah had turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: Pekah son of Remaliah: the king of Israel
decisions.reason: Pekah had seized the throne of Israel in Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) and joined Rezin of Aram against Judah (2 Kings 16:5).

decisions.choice: 120,000: the size of the number
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, the word for "thousand" may name a unit rather than an exact count (see the note at Numbers 1:21).

decisions.choice: sons of valor: able fighting men
decisions.reason: "Sons of valor" describes men of strength and courage, fit for war. The dead were the best of Judah's army.

decisions.choice: because they had forsaken Yahweh: the reason for the defeat
decisions.reason: Forsaking Yahweh is the sin that Chronicles names again and again as the cause of disaster (7:19-22; 12:1, 5; 15:2; 24:20). The God of their fathers is the God who had been faithful to their ancestors.

decisions.choice: valiant men / brave fighting men; ancestors; turned away from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "sons of valor" means (m3) and say "ancestors" for "fathers". Readable adds "soldiers" and names "the people of Judah" as those who had forsaken Yahweh, and says "turned away from" for "forsaken".

records.source: וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֞ג זִכְרִ֣י׀גִּבּ֣וֹר אֶפְרַ֗יִם אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֶת־עַזְרִיקָ֖ם נְגִ֣יד הַבָּ֑יִת וְאֶת־אֶלְקָנָ֖ה מִשְׁנֵ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And killed Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, Maaseiah son of the king, and Azrikam [the] ruler of the house, and Elkanah [the] second of the king.
pieces: Zichri, an Ephraimite warrior, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, who was second to the king.

L.7: And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the son of the king, and Azrikam the ruler of the house, and Elkanah the second to the king.

R.7: Zichri, a warrior from Ephraim, killed three men close to the king: Maaseiah, the king's son; Azrikam, who was in charge of the palace; and Elkanah, the king's second in command.

decisions.choice: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim: a warrior of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Zichri is not named elsewhere. Ephraim, the leading tribe of the north, often stands for the whole northern kingdom (Isaiah 7:2, 5, 8).

decisions.choice: the son of the king: Ahaz's own son, or a royal official
alternatives: a royal official called "the king's son"
decisions.reason: Maaseiah may have been a son of Ahaz. "The king's son" can also be the title of an official of the royal household (1 Kings 22:26; Jeremiah 36:26), and Ahaz was still young (verse 1), so this may be meant instead.

decisions.choice: the ruler of the house: the chief officer of the palace
decisions.reason: The word usually used for a ruler of the people here names the officer over the king's household, like the one "over the house" in 1 Kings 4:6 and 2 Kings 18:18.

decisions.choice: the second to the king: the highest official after the king
decisions.reason: The phrase names the man who ranked next to the king, as Mordecai did under Xerxes (Esther 10:3). With these three deaths the court lost its leading men.

decisions.choice: officer in charge of the palace / in charge of the palace; second in command
decisions.reason: The usual word for this title is "ruler", but here it names a court office, not a ruler of the people (m3), so Balanced and Readable describe the office. Readable adds "three men close to the king" to introduce the list.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁבּוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל מֵֽאֲחֵיהֶ֜ם מָאתַ֣יִם אֶ֗לֶף נָשִׁים֙ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֔וֹת וְגַם־שָׁלָ֥ל רָ֖ב בָּזְז֣וּ מֵהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־הַשָּׁלָ֖ל לְשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: And took captive [the] sons of Israel from their brothers two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters; and also booty much they plundered from them, and they brought the booty to Samaria.
pieces: The Israelites took 200,000 of their own relatives captive, women, sons and daughters. They also seized a great deal of plunder from them and brought the plunder to Samaria.

L.8: And the sons of Israel took captive from their brothers 200,000 women, sons and daughters; and they also plundered much booty from them, and they brought the booty to Samaria.

R.8: The Israelites captured 200,000 of their own relatives, women and children, and took them away. They also took many valuable things from them and brought all of it back to Samaria.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel ... their brothers: the northern army and the people of Judah
decisions.reason: "The sons of Israel" here are the men of the northern kingdom's army. "Their brothers" are the people of Judah, their own kin, descended from the same ancestors (11:4).

decisions.choice: 200,000 women, sons and daughters: the captives were women and children
decisions.reason: The list names women and children only; the men had been killed (verse 6). On the size of the number, see the note on verse 6.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of Israel
decisions.reason: Samaria was the royal city of the northern kingdom (1 Kings 16:24). The captives and plunder were taken there.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel / the Israelites; relatives; women and children (Readable)
decisions.reason: The soldiers are meant, so no alternative form is given for "the sons of Israel". Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers", as at 11:4. Readable says "children" for "sons and daughters".

records.source: וְ֠שָׁם הָיָ֨ה נָבִ֥יא לַֽיהוָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד שְׁמוֹ֒ וַיֵּצֵ֗א לִפְנֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ הַבָּ֣א לְשֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם הִ֠נֵּה בַּחֲמַ֨ת יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה נְתָנָ֣ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַתַּֽהַרְגוּ־בָ֣ם בְזַ֔עַף עַ֥ד לַשָּׁמַ֖יִם הִגִּֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: And there was there a prophet of Yahweh, Oded [was] his name, and he went out before the army that came to Samaria, and he said to them, look, in [the] rage of Yahweh, God of your fathers, against Judah he gave them into your hand, and you killed among them in a fury [that] to the heavens has reached.
pieces: But a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army as it came to Samaria and said to them, "Look, it was because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to you. But you have slaughtered them in a rage that has reached up to heaven.

L.9: But there was a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there, whose name [was] Oded, and he went out before the army that was coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look, because of the rage of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, against Judah, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into your hand; and you have killed among them in a fury that has reached up to heaven.

R.9: But a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} named Oded lived there. He went out to meet the army as it came to Samaria. He said to them, "Listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let you defeat them. But you killed them with such fury that it reached all the way up to heaven.

decisions.choice: Oded: a prophet in Samaria
decisions.reason: This Oded is not the father of the prophet Azariah in Asa's day (15:1, 8). He is a prophet of Yahweh living in the northern kingdom, who goes out to face its returning army.

decisions.choice: God gave them into your hand, but you went too far
decisions.reason: Oded grants that Israel's victory was Yahweh's judgment on Judah, yet the victors went beyond what God intended. The prophets say the same of other nations God used to punish his people (Isaiah 10:5-7; Zechariah 1:15).

decisions.choice: a fury that has reached up to heaven: a slaughter God has seen
decisions.reason: What reaches up to heaven comes before God himself, as the outcry against Sodom did (Genesis 18:20-21) and Israel's guilt in Ezra 9:6. The fury of the slaughter calls for God's judgment.

decisions.choice: and ... and: but ... but
decisions.reason: The first "and" sets the prophet against the scene of verse 8; the second sets the army's slaughter against God's purpose. Both mark a contrast.

decisions.choice: it was because ... that he handed them over / was angry ... so he let you defeat them; But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the cause in a plain clause and say "But" before the slaughter (m4). Readable says "Listen!" for "Look". The speech runs to verse 11.

records.heading: Oded and the captives from Judah

records.source: וְ֠עַתָּה בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֤ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים לִכְבֹּ֛שׁ לַעֲבָדִ֥ים וְלִשְׁפָח֖וֹת לָכֶ֑ם הֲלֹ֤א רַק־אַתֶּם֙ עִמָּכֶ֣ם אֲשָׁמ֔וֹת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And now [the] sons of Judah and Jerusalem you [are] saying to subdue for male slaves and for female slaves for you; [are there] not only with you yourselves guilty things to Yahweh your God?
pieces: And now you intend to force the people of Judah and Jerusalem to become your male and female slaves. But are you not yourselves guilty of wrongs against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?

L.10: And now you are intending to subdue the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah and Jerusalem [as] male slaves and female slaves for yourselves. [Are there] not, with you yourselves, guilty things against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?

R.10: Now you plan to make the men and women of Judah and Jerusalem your slaves. But have you not also sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God?

decisions.choice: you are saying: you intend
decisions.reason: To "say" to do something is to have it in mind to do it (Exodus 2:14; 2 Samuel 21:16).

decisions.choice: to subdue as slaves: what the law forbids among kin
decisions.reason: The law forbids an Israelite to make a fellow Israelite his slave or to rule over him harshly (Leviticus 25:39-46). The people of Judah are the northern army's own kin (verse 8).

decisions.choice: are there not with you yourselves ...: you too are guilty
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". The stress on "you yourselves" turns the charge back on the victors: they punish Judah's sin while carrying guilt of their own.

decisions.choice: guilty things: wrongs that bring guilt before God
decisions.reason: The word names deeds that make a person guilty and liable to punishment (Leviticus 5:19). The leaders take it up again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: male slaves and female slaves / slaves at every level
decisions.reason: Slavery itself is the point here, people forced into servitude, so the word stays "slave" at every level, as the style guide asks for such sentences.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah / the men and women of Judah; guilty of wrongs / sinned
decisions.reason: "Sons of Judah" means the people, and the captives were women and children (verse 8), so Balanced and Readable use inclusive words. Readable says "sinned" for being guilty of wrongs.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה שְׁמָע֔וּנִי וְהָשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ הַשִּׁבְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁבִיתֶ֖ם מֵאֲחֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֛י חֲר֥וֹן אַף־יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And now listen to me and return the captives whom you took captive from your brothers, for [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh [is] on you.
pieces: Now listen to me: send back the captives you have taken from your own relatives, for the fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is upon you."

L.11: And now listen to me and send back the captives whom you have taken captive from your brothers, for the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] upon you."

R.11: So listen to me. Send back the prisoners you took from your own relatives. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is very angry with you."

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger: fierce anger
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures anger as a fire (Exodus 32:12; Numbers 25:4). God's anger is now aimed at Israel.

decisions.choice: upon you: the anger turned from Judah to Israel
decisions.reason: In verse 9 the rage of Yahweh was against Judah. Now, because of their cruelty, it rests on the victors themselves.

decisions.choice: return the captives from your brothers: send them home to their kin
decisions.reason: To return the captives is to set them free and send them back to Judah. "Brothers" means kin, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: relatives; fierce anger / is very angry
decisions.reason: "Relatives" for "brothers" as in verse 8. Readable says the picture of burning anger plainly.

records.gloss: And rose up men from [the] heads of [the] sons of Ephraim, Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, and Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, against those coming from the army.
pieces: Then some of the chiefs of the Ephraimites, Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up to confront those returning from the war.

L.12: And men from the heads of the sons of Ephraim rose up, Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, and Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, against those coming from the army.

R.12: Then some of the leaders of Ephraim stood up against the soldiers coming back from the war. They were Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.

decisions.choice: the heads of the sons of Ephraim: leading men of the north
decisions.reason: These are chiefs of the tribe of Ephraim, which stands for the northern kingdom (verse 7). The four men are not named elsewhere.

decisions.choice: rose up against: stood up to oppose
decisions.reason: To rise up against someone is here to stand in their way, not to attack them. The leaders take the prophet's side.

decisions.choice: those coming from the army: the soldiers returning from the campaign
decisions.reason: The word for "army" also means war or a campaign. Those coming from it are the troops returning from the war with their captives.

decisions.choice: chiefs / leaders; those returning from the war / the soldiers coming back from the war
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "chiefs" or "leaders" for "heads" and say who was returning (m3). Readable gives the names a sentence of their own.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם לֹא־תָבִ֤יאוּ אֶת־הַשִּׁבְיָה֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּי֩ לְאַשְׁמַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים לְהֹסִ֥יף עַל־חַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ וְעַל־אַשְׁמָתֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־רַבָּ֤ה אַשְׁמָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַחֲר֥וֹן אָ֖ף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And they said to them, not you shall bring the captives here, for to guilt of Yahweh upon us you [are] saying to add to our sins and to our guilt; for great [is] guilt to us, and burning of anger [is] upon Israel.
pieces: They said to them, "You must not bring the captives here. What you intend would bring guilt on us before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and add to our sins and our guilt. Our guilt is already great, and fierce anger is upon Israel."

L.13: And they said to them, "You shall not bring the captives here, for you are intending [to bring] guilt against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} upon us, to add to our sins and to our guilt; for our guilt [is] great, and burning anger [is] upon Israel."

R.13: They told the soldiers, "Do not bring the prisoners here! What you plan to do would make us guilty before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It would add to the sins and the guilt we already have. We are already very guilty, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is very angry with Israel."

decisions.choice: for guilt of Yahweh upon us you intend: your plan brings guilt before Yahweh on us
decisions.reason: The sentence is compressed: "to guilt of Yahweh upon us" is the result of what the army intends. Keeping the captives as slaves would add guilt toward Yahweh to the guilt the nation already bears.

decisions.choice: great is our guilt: the leaders confess Israel's sin
decisions.reason: The leaders accept the prophet's charge (verse 10) and admit that Israel already stands under God's fierce anger (verse 11). They act to avoid adding to it.

decisions.choice: sins ... guilt: wrongdoing and the liability it brings
decisions.reason: "Sins" names the wrongs done; "guilt" names the debt of punishment they bring (verse 10). The word for guilt is repeated three times.

decisions.choice: What you intend would ...; already; the LORD is very angry
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the compressed clause a subject (m1) and add "already" to show the guilt is not new. Readable names Yahweh as the one whose anger is meant, as in verse 11, where the Hebrew here says only "burning anger".

records.source: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב הֶֽחָל֗וּץ אֶת־הַשִּׁבְיָה֙ וְאֶת־הַבִּזָּ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְכָל־הַקָּהָֽל׃
records.gloss: And left the armed [men] the captives and the plunder before the princes and all the assembly.
pieces: So the armed men left the captives and the plunder in the presence of the officials and the whole assembly.

L.14: So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the princes and all the assembly.

R.14: So the soldiers left the prisoners and the plunder with the leaders and all the people gathered there.

decisions.choice: the armed men: soldiers equipped for battle
decisions.reason: The word describes men armed and ready for war (Numbers 32:21; Joshua 4:13). Here it is the returning army.

decisions.choice: the princes and all the assembly: a public decision
decisions.reason: The army hands over its captives and plunder before the leaders and the gathered people of Samaria, so the decision is made openly and the people share in it.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders; assembly / the people gathered there
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books. Readable says what the assembly was.

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֩ אֲשֶׁר־נִקְּב֨וּ בְשֵׁמ֜וֹת וַיַּחֲזִ֣יקוּ בַשִּׁבְיָ֗ה וְכָֽל־מַעֲרֻמֵּיהֶם֮ הִלְבִּ֣ישׁוּ מִן־הַשָּׁלָל֒ וַיַּלְבִּשׁ֣וּם וַ֠יַּנְעִלוּם וַיַּאֲכִל֨וּם וַיַּשְׁק֜וּם וַיְסֻכ֗וּם וַיְנַהֲל֤וּם בַּחֲמֹרִים֙ לְכָל־כּוֹשֵׁ֔ל וַיְבִיא֛וּם יְרֵח֥וֹ עִיר־הַתְּמָרִ֖ים אֵ֣צֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּשׁ֖וּבוּ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And rose up the men who were designated by names, and they took hold of the captives, and all their naked [ones] they clothed from the booty; and they clothed them and shod them and fed them and gave them drink and anointed them, and led them on donkeys, every one stumbling, and they brought them [to] Jericho, [the] city of the palm trees, beside their brothers; and they returned [to] Samaria.
pieces: Then the men who had been named for the task got up and took charge of the captives. From the plunder they clothed all among them who were naked. They gave them clothes and sandals, food and drink, and anointed them with oil. They put all who were too weak to walk on donkeys and brought them to their relatives at Jericho, the city of palm trees. Then they went back to Samaria.

L.15: And the men who had been designated by name rose up and took charge of the captives, and all their naked ones they clothed from the booty; and they clothed them and gave them sandals and fed them and gave them drink and anointed them, and they led on donkeys every one who was stumbling, and they brought them [to] Jericho, the city of palm trees, beside their brothers. And they returned [to] Samaria.

R.15: The men who had been chosen by name for this job took charge of the prisoners. They used the plunder to give clothes to all who had none. They gave them clothes and sandals, something to eat and drink, and oil to soothe their skin. They put everyone who was too weak to walk on donkeys. They took them back to their own people at Jericho, the town known for its palm trees. Then they returned to Samaria.

decisions.choice: designated by name: appointed for the task
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of men chosen and named for a duty (Numbers 1:17; 1 Chronicles 12:32; 2 Chronicles 31:19). These may be the four leaders of verse 12, or men they appointed.

decisions.choice: clothed, shod, fed, gave drink, anointed: full care for the captives
decisions.reason: The verbs follow one another to show complete care. Anointing with oil soothed skin worn by travel and hardship and was part of washing and refreshing oneself (Ruth 3:3; 2 Samuel 12:20).

decisions.choice: Jericho, the city of palm trees: a town near the border of Judah
decisions.reason: Jericho is called "the city of palm trees" in Deuteronomy 34:3 and Judges 1:16; 3:13. It lay in the Jordan valley near the boundary between the two kingdoms, where the captives could be handed back to their own people.

decisions.choice: kindness to captured enemies
decisions.reason: Elisha had told the king of Israel to feed captured Aramean soldiers and send them home (2 Kings 6:22-23), and Proverbs 25:21 tells its readers to give food and water to an enemy. The northern leaders act in the same spirit.

decisions.choice: men of Samaria caring for the wounded on the way to Jericho: perhaps echoed in Luke 10:30-37
decisions.reason: In Jesus' story of the Samaritan, a man from Samaria cares for a wounded man on the road to Jericho, treats him with oil, sets him on his animal and brings him to safety. These features match this account closely, but the gospel does not refer to it, and whether the story was meant to recall it cannot be known.

decisions.choice: anointed them with oil / oil to soothe their skin; too weak to walk
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was used and why (m2), and what "stumbling" means here: those too weak to walk. Readable says "the town known for its palm trees" for "the city of palm trees".

records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא שָׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אָחָ֛ז עַל־מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֖וּר לַעְזֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: At the time the that sent the king Ahaz to [the] kings of Assyria to help him.
pieces: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.

L.16: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.

R.16: At that time King Ahaz sent messengers to the kings of Assyria to ask for help.

decisions.choice: the kings of Assyria: plural in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "kings", though verse 20 names only one king, Tilgath-pilneser. The plural may refer to the Assyrian king together with the kings under him, or to the kings of Assyria as a line. Some ancient translations have "the king of Assyria", as in 2 Kings 16:7.

decisions.choice: Ahaz sends to Assyria: told more fully in 2 Kings 16:7
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:7 gives Ahaz's message: "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me." Chronicles gives only the request for help. "At that time" links it to the attacks of verses 5-8 and 17-18.

decisions.choice: to help him: help sought from the wrong place
decisions.reason: "Help" is a key word in this chapter (verses 21, 23). In Chronicles Yahweh helps those who rely on him (14:10; 25:8; 26:7). Ahaz looks for help to Assyria and then to the gods of Aram.

decisions.choice: sent messengers ... to ask for help
decisions.reason: Readable says that Ahaz sent messengers, as 2 Kings 16:7 says, and that he asked for help.

records.heading: Ahaz turns to Assyria

records.source: וְע֥וֹד אֲדוֹמִ֖ים בָּ֑אוּ וַיַּכּ֥וּ בִיהוּדָ֖ה וַיִּשְׁבּוּ־שֶֽׁבִי׃
records.gloss: And again Edomites had come, and they struck in Judah and took captive captives.
pieces: The Edomites had come again, attacked Judah and carried off captives.

L.17: And again Edomites had come, and they struck Judah and took captives.

R.17: The Edomites had attacked Judah again and taken people away as prisoners.

decisions.choice: Edomites had come: the reason Ahaz sent for help
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "Edomites" first, with a verb that gives background. Verses 17-18 explain the pressure on Ahaz that led him to call on Assyria (verse 16).

decisions.choice: again: Edom against Judah once more
decisions.reason: Edom had broken free of Judah under Jehoram (21:8-10) and been beaten by Amaziah (25:11-12). Now it strikes back. 2 Kings 16:6 tells how Edomites took over Elath at this time.

decisions.choice: The Edomites; carried off captives / taken people away as prisoners
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "The Edomites" and give the plain sense of "took captive captives".

records.source: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים פָּשְׁט֗וּ בְּעָרֵ֨י הַשְּׁפֵלָ֣ה וְהַנֶּגֶב֮ לִֽיהוּדָה֒ וַֽ֠יִּלְכְּדוּ אֶת־בֵּֽית־שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ וְאֶת־אַיָּל֜וֹן וְאֶת־הַגְּדֵר֗וֹת וְאֶת־שׂוֹכ֤וֹ וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וְאֶת־תִּמְנָ֣ה וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־גִּמְז֖וֹ וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And Philistines had raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah, and they captured Beth-shemesh and Aijalon and the Gederoth, and Soco and its daughters, and Timnah and its daughters, and Gimzo and its daughters; and they settled there.
pieces: The Philistines had raided the towns of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah. They captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, as well as Soco, Timnah and Gimzo with their villages, and they settled there.

L.18: And the Philistines had made raids on the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah, and they captured Beth-shemesh and Aijalon and Gederoth, and Soco and its villages, and Timnah and its villages, and Gimzo and its villages; and they settled there.

R.18: The Philistines had also raided the towns in Judah's western foothills and in the Negev desert in the south. They captured the towns of Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah and Gimzo, along with the villages around Soco, Timnah and Gimzo. Then the Philistines settled there.

decisions.choice: the Shephelah and the Negev: Judah's western foothills and its dry south
decisions.reason: The Shephelah is the low hill country between the coastal plain and the hills of Judah (1:15). The Negev is the dry land in the south.

decisions.choice: the towns taken: Judah's border towns facing Philistia
decisions.reason: These towns guarded the valleys leading up from the coast into Judah. Uzziah had taken Philistine towns (26:6); now the Philistines take Judah's towns and settle in them. Gimzo is named only here.

decisions.choice: its daughters: its villages
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depend on it (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45).

decisions.choice: the Shephelah (Balanced); western foothills, Negev desert (Readable); villages
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the region's name and Readable describes it, as at 1:15. Balanced and Readable group the towns that have villages, which says the same thing more briefly. Readable names the Philistines again for clarity.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִכְנִ֤יעַ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה בַּעֲב֖וּר אָחָ֣ז מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הִפְרִ֨יעַ֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּמָע֥וֹל מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For had humbled Yahweh Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let run wild in Judah, and acted unfaithfully [with] unfaithfulness against Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brought Judah low on account of Ahaz king of Israel, because he had let Judah throw off all restraint and had been grossly unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.19: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let [the people] run wild in Judah and had acted very unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} humbled Judah because of Ahaz, the king of Israel. Ahaz had let the people of Judah do whatever they wanted, and he had been completely unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Yahweh humbled Judah: the reason for the defeats
decisions.reason: The raids of verses 17-18, like the defeats of verses 5-8, are Yahweh's doing. The verb is the one used when Rehoboam and his leaders "humbled themselves" (12:6-7, 12); here Judah is humbled against its will.

decisions.choice: king of Israel: Ahaz, king of Judah, as king of the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Ahaz ruled Judah. Chronicles often calls Judah's kings and people "Israel", the name of the whole people of God (12:6; 21:2). Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "king of Judah", which may be an easing of the harder reading.

decisions.choice: he had let run wild: let the people throw off restraint
alternatives: he had acted without restraint in Judah
decisions.reason: The verb means to let loose or leave unrestrained. Aaron "let the people run wild" at the golden calf (Exodus 32:25). It may instead mean that Ahaz himself acted without restraint in Judah.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully with unfaithfulness: broke faith completely
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun are set together for emphasis. This is the word Chronicles uses for breaking faith with Yahweh (12:2; 26:16).

decisions.choice: humbled / brought low; let [the people] run wild / throw off all restraint / do whatever they wanted; very / grossly / completely unfaithful
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the people, whom the verb implies (m3). Balanced and Readable say what the verb means in plain words, and render the doubled word for unfaithfulness with a strengthening word. "King of Israel" is kept at every level (m2).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א עָלָ֔יו תִּלְּגַ֥ת פִּלְנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּ֥צַר ל֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א חֲזָקֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And came against him Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he distressed him and not strengthened him.
pieces: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came against him and brought him distress instead of strength.

L.20: And Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him, and he distressed him and did not strengthen him.

R.20: Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, came against Ahaz. He did not make him stronger; he only made trouble for him.

decisions.choice: Tilgath-pilneser: the king called Tiglath-pileser in 2 Kings
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells this king's name Tilgath-pilneser, as at 1 Chronicles 5:6, 26, where 2 Kings spells it Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 16:7). He is the same king, Tiglath-pileser the third of Assyria.

decisions.choice: distressed him: Chronicles' verdict on Assyria's help
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:9 tells that the king of Assyria took Damascus and killed Rezin, as Ahaz had asked. Chronicles does not deny this, but says that in the end Assyria brought Ahaz distress: Judah became a subject state that had to pay heavy tribute (verse 21).

decisions.choice: came against him: or "came to him"
decisions.reason: The little word can mean "to" or "against". With "distressed him" following, the visit is hostile in effect, whatever its purpose.

decisions.choice: distressed him and did not strengthen him
decisions.reason: The first verb comes from the word for distress used again in verse 22. The second is the ordinary word for making strong; the help Ahaz paid for gave him no strength.

decisions.choice: Tilgath-pilneser (Literal); Tiglath-pileser (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Chronicles 5:6: Literal keeps the spelling Chronicles uses; Balanced and Readable use the form found in 2 Kings, so that readers recognize the king (m1). Balanced joins the two verbs as "distress instead of strength".

records.source: כִּֽי־חָלַ֤ק אָחָז֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּן֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְלֹ֥א לְעֶזְרָ֖ה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For had taken a share Ahaz [of] the house of Yahweh and the house of the king and the princes, and he gave [it] to [the] king of Assyria; and not for help [it was] to him.
pieces: Ahaz took a share of the wealth of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, of the royal palace and of the officials, and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did him no good.

L.21: For Ahaz took a share from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king and the princes, and he gave [it] to the king of Assyria; but [it was] not of help to him.

R.21: Ahaz took valuable things from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from the royal palace and from his leaders, and he gave them to the king of Assyria. But this did not help him.

decisions.choice: took a share: stripped part of their wealth
decisions.reason: The verb means to divide or take a portion. Ahaz took part of the riches of the temple, the palace and the leading men to pay the king of Assyria.

decisions.choice: the payment to Assyria: as 2 Kings 16:8, with more added
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:8 says Ahaz sent the silver and gold of the temple and the palace treasuries to the king of Assyria as a bribe. Chronicles adds the wealth of the princes and says that the payment brought no help (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the princes: their houses or their wealth
decisions.reason: "The princes" follows "the house of the king" as a third object: the wealth of the royal officials was taken as well.

decisions.choice: the wealth of / valuable things; officials / leaders; it did him no good / this did not help him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was taken (m1). "Princes" follows the wording kept for this word: "officials" at Balanced, "leaders" at Readable. "Temple" and "royal palace" at Readable as these books say.

records.source: וּבְעֵת֙ הָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ וַיּ֖וֹסֶף לִמְע֣וֹל בַּיהוָ֑ה ה֖וּא הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז׃
records.gloss: And in [the] time of distressing to him he added to act unfaithfully against Yahweh, he, the king Ahaz.
pieces: In his time of distress this same King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: And in the time of his distress he became still more unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this same King Ahaz.

R.22: When Ahaz was in trouble, he became even more unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That was the kind of man King Ahaz was.

decisions.choice: in his distress he grew more unfaithful: the opposite of what distress should bring
decisions.reason: Solomon prayed that in distress the people would turn to Yahweh (6:28-31), and in their distress Asa's people sought him (15:4). Manasseh later humbled himself in his distress (33:12). Ahaz did the reverse.

decisions.choice: he, King Ahaz: the writer points to the man
decisions.reason: The sentence ends with "he, King Ahaz", like a finger pointed at him: this is the kind of king he was.

decisions.choice: he added to act unfaithfully: he became more unfaithful still
decisions.reason: "Added" means he did more of it. The word for unfaithfulness is the one in verse 19.

decisions.choice: this same King Ahaz; That was the kind of man King Ahaz was
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "he, King Ahaz" at the end as "this same King Ahaz"; Balanced moves it to be the subject; Readable gives the pointing phrase a sentence of its own (m2).

records.source: וַיִּזְבַּ֗ח לֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י דַרְמֶשֶׂק֮ הַמַּכִּ֣ים בּוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּ֠י אֱלֹהֵ֤י מַלְכֵֽי־אֲרָם֙ הֵ֚ם מַעְזְרִ֣ים אוֹתָ֔ם לָהֶ֥ם אֲזַבֵּ֖חַ וְיַעְזְר֑וּנִי וְהֵ֛ם הָֽיוּ־ל֥וֹ לְהַכְשִׁיל֖וֹ וּלְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he sacrificed to [the] gods of Damascus who struck him, and he said, because [the] gods of [the] kings of Aram, they help them, to them I will sacrifice, and they will help me; and they were to him to make stumble him and all Israel.
pieces: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, and said, "Since the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them so that they will help me." But they brought ruin on him and on all Israel.

L.23: And he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had struck him, and he said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram, they help them, to them I will sacrifice, and they will help me." But they became to him [a cause] to make him stumble, and all Israel.

R.23: He offered sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, the gods of the people who had defeated him. He said, "The gods of the kings of Aram help them. So I will offer sacrifices to them, and they will help me too." But these gods only brought ruin on Ahaz and on all Israel.

decisions.choice: the gods of Damascus who struck him: Ahaz's mistaken reasoning
decisions.reason: Ahaz thinks the gods of Aram gave Aram its victory. The writer has already said that it was Yahweh who gave Ahaz into the hand of the king of Aram (verse 5). The help he seeks from these gods brings only ruin.

decisions.choice: sacrifice to the gods of Damascus: compare the altar from Damascus
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:10-16 tells how Ahaz copied an altar he saw in Damascus and made it the main altar of the temple. Chronicles speaks of his worship of the gods of Damascus themselves.

decisions.choice: to make him stumble, and all Israel: the downfall of the king and his people
decisions.reason: To cause to stumble is to bring about a fall. "All Israel" here is the people of Judah, as Chronicles uses the name (verse 19).

decisions.choice: the gods of the people who had defeated him; too; these gods only brought ruin
decisions.reason: Readable says that it was the people of Damascus who defeated Ahaz, whose gods he credited with the victory (m1), and adds "too" to show his reasoning. Balanced and Readable say "ruin" for causing to stumble (m3).

records.source: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף אָחָ֜ז אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיְקַצֵּץ֙ אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּסְגֹּ֖ר אֶת־דַּלְת֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֧וֹ מִזְבְּח֛וֹת בְּכָל־פִּנָּ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And gathered Ahaz [the] vessels of [the] house of God, and he cut up [the] vessels of [the] house of God, and he shut [the] doors of [the] house of Yahweh, and he made for himself altars in every corner in Jerusalem.
pieces: Ahaz collected the vessels of the house of God and cut them in pieces. He shut the doors of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made himself altars on every street corner in Jerusalem.

L.24: And Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God, and he cut up the vessels of the house of God, and he shut the doors of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he made for himself altars in every corner in Jerusalem.

R.24: Ahaz collected the bowls and other objects used in God's temple, and he cut them into pieces. He closed the doors of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he set up altars for himself on every street corner in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: cutting up the vessels: more than 2 Kings 16:17 tells
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:17 says Ahaz cut off the panels of the bronze stands and took down the Sea. Chronicles says more broadly that he cut up the vessels of the temple, and adds that he shut its doors, which Kings does not mention.

decisions.choice: he shut the doors of the house of Yahweh: the worship of Yahweh stopped
decisions.reason: With the doors shut, the lamps went out and the incense and burnt offerings ceased (29:7). Hezekiah's first act as king was to open the doors again (29:3).

decisions.choice: altars in every corner: altars throughout the city
decisions.reason: "Every corner" means the street corners of Jerusalem: there were altars everywhere except at the temple. Jeremiah 11:13 speaks of altars as many as Jerusalem's streets.

decisions.choice: cut them in pieces; bowls and other objects; street corner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" instead of repeating "the vessels of the house of God". Readable names the kind of vessels meant. Both say "street corner" (m3).

records.source: וּבְכָל־עִ֨יר וָעִ֤יר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה בָמ֔וֹת לְקַטֵּ֖ר לֵֽאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיַּכְעֵ֕ס אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And in every city and city of Judah he made high places to make smoke to gods other, and he provoked to anger Yahweh, God of his fathers.
pieces: In each and every town of Judah he set up high places for burning incense to other gods, and he provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors, to anger.

L.25: And in every city, city of Judah, he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his fathers, to anger.

R.25: In every single town in Judah he built hilltop shrines for burning incense to other gods. In this way he made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors, angry.

decisions.choice: every city and city: each and every town
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun means "every single one" (as in Esther 8:9, "province and province").

decisions.choice: provoked to anger with other gods: as Deuteronomy warned
decisions.reason: Moses' song says that Israel would provoke Yahweh with strange gods (Deuteronomy 32:16, 21). Kings uses the same verb for the sins of Jeroboam and later kings (1 Kings 14:9; 16:2).

decisions.choice: every city, city / each and every town / every single town; high places / hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Each level says the repeated noun its own way (m1). "High places" and "hilltop shrines" are the wording kept in these books.

records.source: וְיֶ֤תֶר דְּבָרָיו֙ וְכָל־דְּרָכָ֔יו הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of his matters and all his ways, the first and the last, look, they [are] written in [the] book of [the] kings of Judah and Israel.
pieces: The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

L.26: And the rest of his matters and all his ways, the first and the last, look, they [are] written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

R.26: Everything else Ahaz did and all his ways, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

decisions.choice: the sources formula, in Chronicles' form; parallel to 2 Kings 16:19
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:19 refers to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah". Chronicles names "the book of the kings of Judah and Israel", as at 16:11, and adds "all his ways, first and last", that is, his whole reign.

decisions.choice: look: pointing the reader to the record
decisions.reason: The word draws attention, as if pointing to where the record can be found.

decisions.choice: "look" left out; the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel (Balanced); the book of the kings of Judah and Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 16:11: Balanced and Readable carry the pointing word by the plain statement, and Balanced writes the source as a title.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אָחָ֜ז עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֤הוּ בָעִיר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הֱבִיאֻ֔הוּ לְקִבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הֽוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Ahaz with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, for not they brought him into [the] tombs of [the] kings of Israel; and reigned Hezekiah his son in his place.
pieces: Then Ahaz rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem; but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.

L.27: And Ahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

R.27: Then Ahaz died. He was buried in the city of Jerusalem, but he was not laid in the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king after him.

decisions.choice: buried in Jerusalem but not in the royal tombs: as 2 Kings 16:20, with a difference
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 16:20 says Ahaz was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Chronicles says he was buried in the city, in Jerusalem, but not brought into the tombs of the kings. Both can be true: he lay in the city but outside the royal tombs, a mark of dishonor given also to Jehoram and Joash (21:20; 24:25).

decisions.choice: the kings of Israel: the kings of Judah
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, Chronicles calls Judah's kings "the kings of Israel": the royal tombs were in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as at 2 Kings 16:20.

decisions.choice: for they did not bring him: an explanation that marks a contrast
decisions.reason: The word that introduces the clause explains "in the city": in the city, that is, not in the tombs of the kings.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died; for / but
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded throughout Kings and Chronicles; Readable does not add "with his ancestors" because the Hebrew does not name a burial with them. Balanced and Readable say "but" for the contrast (m4). The close of 2 Kings 16:20 is kept for Hezekiah.
